```{r}
library(WDI)
library(tidyverse)

wdi_gini <- WDI(
  country = c("US", "CA", "GB", "FR", "BR"),
  indicator = c("SI.POV.GINI", "SP.DYN.IMRT.IN"),
  start = 2022,
  end = 2022
)

dim(wdi_gini)
```

```{r}
wdi_gini <- WDI(
  country = "all",
  indicator = c("SI.POV.GINI", "SP.DYN.IMRT.IN"),
  start = 2022,
  end = 2022,
  extra = TRUE   # adds region and income group columns
)

dim(wdi_gini)
```

```{r}
clean_gini <- wdi_gini %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(SI.POV.GINI),
    !is.na(SP.DYN.IMRT.IN)
  )

dim(clean_gini)
```

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(tidyverse)
library(countrycode)

graph_gini <- clean_gini %>%
  rename(
    Gini = SI.POV.GINI,
    Infant_Mortality = SP.DYN.IMRT.IN
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Continent = countrycode(iso3c, "iso3c", "continent"),
    # World Bank income group, ordered Low -> High so legends and panels sort correctly
    Income = factor(
      income,
      levels = c("Low income", "Lower middle income",
                 "Upper middle income", "High income")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Continent), !is.na(Income))

dim(graph_gini)
```

```{r}
ui_gini <- fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Income Inequality vs. Infant Mortality (2022)"),

  # Colour the points by continent or by World Bank income group
  radioButtons(
    "colour_by",
    "Colour points by:",
    choices = c("Continent" = "Continent", "Income group" = "Income"),
    inline = TRUE
  ),

  # Show one panel per income group, to see whether the relationship
  # holds at every income level
  checkboxInput("split_income", "Split by income group", value = FALSE),

  plotlyOutput("gini_scatterplot", height = "auto"),

  # Strength of the relationship: Spearman correlation and number of countries
  h4("Correlation (Spearman)"),
  tableOutput("cor_table")
)
```

```{r}
server_gini <- function(input, output) {

  output$gini_scatterplot <- renderPlotly({

    p <- ggplot(
      graph_gini,
      aes(
        x = Gini,
        y = Infant_Mortality,
        # .data[[...]] picks the column whose name is stored in input$colour_by
        color = .data[[input$colour_by]],
        text = paste0(
          "Country: ", country,
          "<br>Continent: ", Continent,
          "<br>Income group: ", Income,
          "<br>Gini Index: ", round(Gini, 1),
          "<br>Infant Mortality: ",
          round(Infant_Mortality, 1),
          " deaths per 1,000 live births"
        )
      )
    ) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5) +
      geom_smooth(
        # group = 1: one line through all points; text = NULL: the line has no tooltip
        aes(group = 1, text = NULL),
        method = "lm",
        formula = y ~ x,
        se = FALSE,
        color = "black"
      ) +
      scale_y_log10() +
      labs(
        title = "Gini Coefficient vs. Infant Mortality (2022)",
        x = "Gini Index (0–100)",
        y = "Infant Mortality (per 1,000 live births, log scale)",
        color = if (input$colour_by == "Income") "Income group" else "Continent"
      )

    # One panel per income group (each with its own trend line)
    if (input$split_income) {
      p <- p + facet_wrap(~ Income)
    }

    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text", height = if (input$split_income) 700 else 450)

  })

  output$cor_table <- renderTable({

    # Spearman correlation, r and p-value, for one set of countries
    spearman_row <- function(data, group_name) {
      # A correlation needs at least 3 countries; otherwise report n only
      if (nrow(data) < 3) {
        return(tibble(Group = group_name, Countries = nrow(data),
                      `Spearman r` = NA_real_, `p-value` = NA_character_))
      }
      test <- cor.test(data$Gini, data$Infant_Mortality,
                       method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
      tibble(
        Group       = group_name,
        Countries   = nrow(data),
        `Spearman r` = round(unname(test$estimate), 2),
        # as text, so tiny values show as "<0.001" instead of being rounded to 0.00
        `p-value`   = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
      )
    }

    # All countries, plus one row per income group when the chart is split
    result <- spearman_row(graph_gini, "All countries")

    if (input$split_income) {
      by_income <- graph_gini %>%
        group_by(Income) %>%
        group_modify(~ spearman_row(.x, as.character(.y$Income))) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        select(-Income)
      result <- bind_rows(result, by_income)
    }

    result
  })
}

shinyApp(ui_gini, server_gini)
```
